scope: 15 selected sources directly relevant to circuit/layout decisions; not exhaustive or a performance ranking

records.title: Active-Matrix GaN Micro Light-Emitting Diode Display With Unprecedented Brightness
records.process: 0.35 µm silicon CMOS driver; sapphire-grown 450 nm InGaN/GaN LED array
records.architecture: Pitch-matched CMOS switching drivers, separate LED_VDD/GND/LED_GND terminals, bump bonding; grid power rails and larger drive devices studied against prior linear rails

data.label: Array luminance
data.conditions: Device B patterns/full-array section at 3.6 V, approximately 7.7 mA/pixel; pixel pitch 100 µm. This is not our 20 µm/100 µA operating point.

data.label: Realized single-pixel current
data.conditions: Approximately 300 mA in the generation-2 assembly, limited by LED; NOT demonstrated for all pixels simultaneously.

data.label: Simultaneously operated array section
data.conditions: 1×1 mm² section operated at total current 900 mA; different operating point from 300 mA single pixel.

records.locator: IEEE TED 62(6), pp.1918–1925; Section II.A CMOS Layout pp.1919–1920; Fig.2 and Table I; Fig.3 pp.1920; Section II.D/Fig.7 p.1922.
records.supports: Silicon CMOS can drive GaN LEDs; physical PG and LED n-contact geometry alter simultaneous-pixel behavior and voltage headroom.
records.does_not_support: No proof of our mirror precision, our model validity, 20 µm pixel behavior, or a generally applicable current/rate ceiling.
records.notes: Official author-university full text reviewed. PDF includes a cover sheet: journal p.1919 is PDF page 3. High brightness is conditioned on a large 100 µm-pitch device. Avoid converting 10 ns pulse operation into a communication BER claim.
records.cn_guide: 看CMOS与LED如何连接；高亮度和单pixel大电流不是全阵列同时工作的证明。
records.reuse: Link/cite bibliographic identity and factual values with attribution; no source figures reproduced

records.title: GF180MCU Design Manual 7.7 Poly2 — minimum channel lengths for 3.3 V, 5 V and 6 V CMOS
records.process: GF180MCU planar silicon CMOS design rules
records.architecture: Poly2 gate geometry under each voltage class

data.label: 3.3 V NMOS/PMOS minimum drawn channel lengths
data.conditions: Poly2 rule PL.2 and opening paragraph; both LV devices.

data.label: 6 V NMOS/PMOS minimum drawn channel lengths
data.conditions: Poly2 rule PL.2 and note 1; 6 V operating class, not the 5 V variant.

data.label: 5 V NMOS/PMOS minimum drawn channel lengths
data.conditions: Poly2 rule PL.2; do not mistake wider model geometry coverage for 6 V layout allowance.

records.locator: Opening paragraph; Poly2 RULES PL.2; note 1.
records.supports: Same silicon process has distinct voltage-dependent device geometries; our 4 µm mirrors and 1 µm switches are intentionally longer than minimum.
records.does_not_support: 180 nm process name is not the Lmin of our 6 V MOS; shrinking L is not automatically an improvement in mirror precision or reliability.
records.notes: Official public page spells NNMOS; interpretation NMOS is unambiguous in its rule table. W/L in a FET call must use drawn design dimensions, not effective channel dimensions.
records.reuse: Link/cite bibliographic identity and factual values with attribution; no source figures reproduced

records.title: GF180MCU Electrical Specifications 5.3 — Gate oxide capacitance
records.process: 3.3 V and 6 V GF180MCU gate oxide specifications
records.architecture: Unit-area oxide capacitance specification; not total gate/input/pixel capacitance

data.label: Typical 3.3 V gate Cox
data.conditions: Both N and P gate poly; min/max 3.4/5.4 fF/µm².

data.label: Typical 6 V gate Cox
data.conditions: Both N and P gate poly; min/max 1.8/2.8 fF/µm².

records.locator: Section 5.3 table, COX (Poly) 3.3V and COX (Poly) 6V rows.
records.supports: Thicker-gate category has lower unit-area Cox; total transistor charge depends on area, bias, overlap and junctions as well.
records.does_not_support: Lower Cox by itself does not establish faster driver speed; do not claim thick oxide inherently gives larger unit-area capacitance.
records.notes: No inference of exact chemical gate dielectric/material stack is needed or made. Speed comparisons require actual gm/charge/voltage/loading and models.
records.reuse: Link/cite bibliographic identity and factual values with attribution; no source figures reproduced

records.title: GF180MCU Design Manual 14.1 — Chip operating conditions and thin/thick gate-oxide reliability limits
records.process: GF180MCU 3.3 V LV thin oxide and 5 V/6 V higher-voltage thick gate
records.architecture: Reliability depends on terminal-to-terminal stress, exposure time/duty and operating conditions; nominal supply class is not a universal terminal rating

data.label: Thin-oxide DC gate-to-other-node absolute limit
data.conditions: Section 14.1.4.2; applies between gate and any other FET node, not simply chip supply voltage.

data.label: Nominal voltage classes
data.conditions: Section 14.1.2: 3.3 V LV, 5/6 V HV; drain HCI and gate-oxide constraints must both be satisfied.

records.supports: 6 V vs 3.3 V is a voltage/gate-oxide device choice within silicon CMOS; startup and coupled-node overshoot need terminal stress review.
records.does_not_support: Do not treat a model solving at a voltage as proof of long-term reliability; 3.3 V thin-oxide devices cannot simply replace our 6 V output without a voltage-domain design.
records.notes: Public text lists a thick-gate DC value as 6.5V/6V for the 5V/6V process; avoid rearranging those into a universal 6.6 V gate rating. HCI and TDDB lifetime/duty constraints are separate. No unpublished material stack inferred.
records.reuse: Link/cite bibliographic identity and factual values with attribution; no source figures reproduced

records.title: All-GaN-Based Monolithic MIS-HEMT Integrated Micro-LED Pixels for Active-Matrix Displays
records.authors: Yuta Furusawa, Wentao Cai, Heajong Cheong, Yoshio Honda and Hiroshi Amano
records.process: Single MOVPE growth on sapphire; AlGaN/GaN 2DEG injects directly into LED quantum wells; 4-nm ALD Al2O3 MIS gate; carbon-doped GaN buffer in matrix version.
records.architecture: Two MIS-HEMTs + one LED per pixel, select and drive; fabricated 2×2 matrix. Drive is normally-on; negative row/column biases needed for selective off.
records.evidence_class: fabricated electrical and optical prototype; photodiode-derived optical estimate and assumed-pitch normalization

data.label: maximum optical output estimate
data.conditions: §2.1/Fig.4b linear LED-HEMT; photodiode area 100 mm² at 10 mm below device; finite collection solid angle ~1 sr; not integrating-sphere total power.

data.label: calculated pixel-area power density
data.conditions: §2.1: 50 µW divided by assumed 100 µm×100 µm pixel pitch, not by 18 µm×15 µm LED active area; not photometric luminance.

records.supports: GaN-based transistor and LED can share an epitaxial/material platform; individual devices in a monolithic 2×2 matrix can be addressed.
records.does_not_support: Does not prove mature GaN display manufacturing, low-voltage normally-off operation, storage-capacitor retention, array uniformity or communication data rate.
records.notes: §2.4 describes parasitic Schottky leakage through wiring/buffer, and proposes added insulation before useful 2T1C retention/large-array scaling. Gate negative-off requirements materially differ from silicon CMOS logic.
records.cn_guide: 了解真正的GaN driver原型；normally-on、负压关断与布线漏电改变系统要求。
records.reuse: Link/cite bibliographic identity and factual values with attribution; no source figures reproduced

records.title: Wafer-scale organic-on-III-V monolithic heterogeneous integration for active-matrix micro-LED displays
records.process: Solution-processed organic semiconductor small-molecule/polymer blend; top-gate bottom-contact OTFT, polymer dielectric; organic-last process on GaN LED plane with post-OTFT vias, ≤150°C integration.
records.architecture: 2T1C active matrix with switch TFT, drive TFT and storage capacitor; 48×48 panel fabricated.
records.evidence_class: measured TFTs, fabricated pixel/panel and dynamic optical display

data.label: panel resolution
data.conditions: Fig.4b–e; 100 µm×100 µm pitch; LED 28 µm×26 µm; 48×48 demonstration.

data.label: demonstrated dynamic frame rate
data.conditions: §Display integration/Fig.4e and Supplementary Movie1, words/firework display.

records.locator: PDF pp.2–3 integration/electrical performance; pp.5–6 Fig.4/display integration; p.6 Methods material stack.
records.supports: MicroLED light-emitter material and transistor channel material can differ; low-temperature integration/interconnect quality can matter more than the highest mobility.
records.does_not_support: Does not establish GHz links, industrial lifetime/yield or equivalence to CMOS/TFTs under matched biases and pixel area.
records.notes: OTFT is not OLED. The demonstrated light emitter remains inorganic GaN. Separate high-current stress geometry from the small pixel geometry; do not transfer wide-device reliability measurements to all pixels.
records.cn_guide: organic TFT不是OLED：电子驱动层为有机材料，发光器件仍是GaN LED。
records.reuse: Link/cite bibliographic identity and factual values with attribution; no source figures reproduced

records.title: A Micro-LED PWM pixel circuit achieving stable ultra-low-gray expression through drain-reservoir feedback
records.process: Coplanar top-gate p-LTPS and a-IGZO TFT measured transfer/output curves; HSPICE RPI models fitted with TFT parasitics included.
records.architecture: 14T4C: 4T1C CCG, 6T1C PWM, 3T1C feedback, 1T1C drain reservoir; separates PWM drain node from current-source gate during feedback delay.
records.evidence_class: individual TFT characteristics measured; complete pixel operation and nominal layout simulated/designed

data.label: simulated LED-current fall time
data.conditions: Fig.5; 90%→10% of peak current; HSPICE, 640×360 target at 120 Hz; not measured optical fall time.

data.label: simulated average-current error
data.conditions: γ=2.2 8-bit mapping, down to gray 6G, driving-TFT VTH shifts ±0.5 V; lower codes not established.

records.supports: Fast edges alone are insufficient: PWM delay, feedback activation and low-gray voltage margin need joint compensation.
records.does_not_support: Does not show an 8-bit measured display, reliable codes below 6G, optical validation, physical DRC/LVS or high-speed communication.
records.notes: Proposed layout area/PPI is design evidence only. This is a useful near-project question: distinguish edge fall time from pulse-area error and data-to-time conversion error.
records.cn_guide: 学习短脉冲下降与低灰阶积分误差；所报动态结果是拟合器件模型后的HSPICE。
records.reuse: Link/cite bibliographic identity and factual values with attribution; no source figures reproduced

records.title: Three-dimensional monolithic micro-LED display driven by atomically thin transistor matrix
records.source_type: peer-reviewed research article; author institutional PDF
records.process: Monolayer CVD MoS2 grown separately then transferred onto GaN LED plane; backgate/Al2O3 stack, ultraclean Au-supported transfer; low-temperature BEOL integration, not low-temperature MoS2 growth.
records.architecture: 1T1D pixel; one MoS2 driving FET and one LED, independently addressed gate/data lines with progressive FPGA scanning; fabricated 32×32 array.
records.evidence_class: measured FETs, single-pixel electrical/optical tests and display prototype; bandwidth and maximum scan-rate potential partly inferred/designed

data.label: prototype pixel density
data.conditions: 32×32 array; 20 µm pitch; 10 µm LED; FPGA progressive scan. Resolution is geometric, not full-array yield.

data.label: measured single-pixel pulse operation
data.conditions: Fig.3e; synchronized Vdata/Vg; equipment-limited 330 ns voltage edges; electrical delay components 240 ns rising +170 ns falling.

records.locator: PDF journal pp.1233–1235 Figs.2–4; Methods appended PDFp.7, integration/material characterization.
records.supports: A non-silicon channel can drive an inorganic LED with a monolithic BEOL architecture; clean transfer/contact and interconnect quality are crucial.
records.does_not_support: Does not demonstrate Gbit/s data link, measured 2.4 MHz optical −3dB bandwidth, high production yield or an entire low-temperature-grown material stack.
records.notes: 2.4 MHz is inferred from inverse 410 ns total delay, not measured link bandwidth. MoS2 growth typically1000°C; post-LED integration about200°C. QR demonstration identifies128 should-lit open pixels and2 short pixels, then repairs failed pixels in image for QR decode; these are not a 1024-pixel global-yield denominator.
records.cn_guide: 学习MoS₂与GaN三维集成；实测频率、delay推算、失败pixel和制造温度分开。
records.reuse: Link/cite bibliographic identity and factual values with attribution; no source figures reproduced

records.title: 1.5 Gbit/s Multi-Channel Visible Light Communications Using CMOS-Controlled GaN-Based LEDs

process.driver: 16 x 16 CMOS driver cells, 100 x 100 um cells; foundry/node not explicitly established in reviewed text
process.LED: Blue 450 nm GaN, 16 x 16 array; 99 x 99 um square pixels, 100 um pitch, common n-contact/individual p-contact; flip-chip bonded

records.architecture: Each CMOS cell is a high-speed digitally triggered switch applying LED bias. Four independent data inputs with a shared clock; source data instruments feed actual CMOS driver cells. It is not direct instrument drive of the LED.

data.label: Simultaneous per-channel rate
data.conditions: Four simultaneously modulated pixels; OOK-NRZ PRBS 2^7-1; input trigger 0-2 V; applied LED bias 6.5 V

data.label: Measured aggregate rate
data.conditions: Four x 375 Mbit/s; distinct from a single-lane 1.5 Gbit/s result

data.label: Author-defined error-free criterion
data.conditions: Paper defines error-free as BER less than this bound; zero observed errors must not be rewritten as BER=0

data.label: Four-channel received-power penalty
data.conditions: Compared with one-channel operation at the stated rate/error-free criterion

records.locator: Griffith PDF 7 pages including cover. PDF p3: device and CMOS cells; p4: frequency response, OOK setup and Fig4; p5: BER/Fig5 and electrical crosstalk/ground bounce; p6: conclusion. Journal pages 1211-1216.
supports: Actual CMOS driver parallel operation can reach aggregate Gbit/s
Supply routing can couple otherwise independent channels
Parallel rate must state channel denominator
does_not_support: Proposed 16 x 375 Mbit/s = 6 Gbit/s scaling was measured
This driver architecture has 1.5 Gbit/s single-lane capability
The paper's LED bias or driver implementation can be adopted without its own voltage/safety model
notes: Full PDF obtained read-only in memory using public repository; no source PDF copied into this project. Optical crosstalk controlled by selecting separated pixels; electrical coupling still observed.
records.cn_guide: 优先看四路并发与ground bounce；1.5 Gbit/s是四路总值。
records.reuse: Link/cite bibliographic identity and factual values with attribution; no source figures reproduced

records.title: High Speed Integrated Digital to Light Converter for Short Range Visible Light Communication
records.authors: Aravind V. N. Jalajakumari et al.

process.driver: CMOS; process node not directly stated in reviewed manuscript
process.LED: 16 common-anode 450 nm InGaN/GaN MicroLEDs, 24 um diameter; individual cathodes; wire bonded to CMOS driver

records.architecture: 4-bit LVDS input to 16-bit thermometer code; 16 NMOS current-source/cascode/differential-switch cells steer current between LED main branch and dummy branch. Each cell adjustable 1-16 mA; dummy rail 1.8 V.

data.label: Reported input/current-cell switching capability
data.conditions: Section II-A architecture capability; not a 500 Mbit/s optical BER result

data.label: Measured OFDM link data rate
data.conditions: SEG2 contact scheme; 200 MHz chip clock, 16-QAM OFDM, CP=10, FFT=128, 5 cm link, BER threshold 1e-3; APD/TIA and offline scope/Matlab processing

data.label: SEG2 link bias per cell
data.conditions: Section III setup, external LED supply 8.2 V; this paper's load and optical setup, not present repository's 100 uA design point

records.locator: 4-page accepted manuscript: p2 sections II-A/B/C and III architecture, 24 um LED and supplies; p3 setup receiver/data handling; p4 IV-B data transmission and finite stream length. Journal 29(1), 118-121; online Nov 2016, issue Jan 2017.
supports: CMOS NMOS cells can implement differential current steering and cascode for a MicroLED transmitter
Switching clock, optical bandwidth and communication rate are different observables
Dummy-branch current remains relevant to energy accounting
does_not_support: Six-MOS low-rate pixel topology already supports this waveform
16 emitting elements equal 16 independent communication lanes
500 MHz architecture capability equals measured 500 MHz optical bandwidth
BER=0 or a long-run BER claim
notes: Institution metadata variants state 85% efficiency while reviewed manuscript computes 70%; efficiency omitted from this index's data pending version reconciliation. Manuscript states 32 kbits for its OFDM stream; keep finite sampling limits.
records.cn_guide: 优先学current steering、dummy与cascode；16颗LED属于同一DLC而非16个lane。

records.title: A Multi-Gigabit/sec Integrated Multiple-Input Multiple-Output VLC Demonstrator

process.driver: Austria Micro Systems 0.18 um CMOS, four 8-bit current-steering DAC channels per chip; two chips for four-channel experiment
process.LED: 450 nm GaN; 39 um MicroLEDs, common p-contact and individual n-contact, nine clusters with 750 um cluster spacing

records.architecture: CMOS DAC/FPGA-driven four-channel setup and independent AWG-driven four/nine-channel setups. A 3 x 3 CMOS APD/TIA receiver and imaging optics complete the link.

data.label: CMOS-DAC four-channel aggregate raw rate range
data.conditions: Section IV-C; 4-PAM, 1 m link, approximately 45 mA average per LED, varying horizontal displacement; FPGA/sample-rate limitations and offline filtering/equalization/decoding

data.label: CMOS-DAC four-channel aggregate net rate range
data.conditions: Author-reported approximate rates after 7% FEC overhead; not per lane

data.label: AWG-driven nine-channel aggregate raw rate
data.conditions: Sections III and IV-D; DAC driver replaced by Agilent 81150A AWG; 0.5 m; 8-PAM with DFE and joint MIMO decoding; not CMOS ASIC throughput

data.label: AWG-driven maximum per-channel rate
data.conditions: Nine-channel instrument-driven link; heterogeneous channel results summed to 7.48 Gbit/s

data.label: Rate-evaluation BER threshold
data.conditions: Section IV; criterion used to report achievable rates, not an uncoded zero-error criterion

records.locator: Coventry PDF 8 pages including cover: p3 II-A driver process; p4 II-B/C LED/APD; p5 III expressly separates CMOS and AWG systems, IV-A frequency response; p6 IV-C CMOS-DAC results/Fig9; p7 IV-D nine-channel AWG result. Journal 35(20), 4358-4365.
supports: A 0.18 um CMOS MicroLED driver was used in measured aggregate Gbit/s operation
Independent stimulus and receiver bottlenecks must be separated from emitter/ASIC limits
